conventions.units: Meters (Blender units). World coordinates are Blender world coordinates (z up).
conventions.pixel_coordinates: x to the right, y down, (0, 0) = center of the top-left pixel (OpenCV).
conventions.intrinsics: K is the OpenCV camera matrix for the image size above.
conventions.extrinsics: opencv_world_to_camera: x_camera = R @ x_world + t, camera x right, y down, z forward (OpenCV). blender_camera_to_world: Blender camera matrix (camera looks along -z, y up).
conventions.depth_exr: float32, single channel (Y). Distance along the camera viewing axis in meters (z in OpenCV camera coordinates, not the distance to the camera center). 0 = no surface.
conventions.depth_png: 16-bit, normalized per image: 65535 = nearest, 1 = farthest, 0 = no surface. The range in meters is in the sample metadata (depth_range_m), so the PNG can be converted to meters.
conventions.normal_png: 16-bit RGB, camera-space unit normals encoded as (n + 1) / 2 in Blender/OpenGL camera axes: x right, y UP, z TOWARDS the camera. For OpenCV camera axes, negate y and z. 0 = no surface.
conventions.mask_image_diff: 8-bit, 255 = defect. Image-difference mask: made from the difference of the defective and reference images (threshold + morphology), so it depends on lighting and noise.
conventions.mask_depth_diff: 8-bit, 255 = defect. Depth-difference mask: pixels where the visible surface moved by more than 1 micrometer along the viewing axis (or appeared/disappeared) because of the defects, from the depth of the reference and the defective render. Independent of lighting and noise. Each pixel is judged at a single point (the first render sample), so edges are not anti-aliased. mask_depth_diff_pixel_count = 0 in the sample metadata means the defect is not visible from that camera.
conventions.reference: The same surface rendered before the defects were added (same camera, same lighting). Saved only when image-difference masks are created.
